questions.question: Which of the following is a unitary feature of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution: Single Citizenship is a unitary feature of the Indian Constitution. In a strict federal system (like the US), citizens have both national and state citizenship. India, however, provides only one citizenship to foster national integration. Note: Written Constitution, Distribution of Power, and Rigidity are considered federal features.

questions.question: Which is NOT correct about India’s Prime Minister?
questions.option_1: He is appointed by the President of India.
questions.option_2: He is the head of the government.
questions.option_3: He can be removed if a no confidence motion is passed by both the Houses of Parliament with 2/3rd majority.
questions.option_4: He is the leader of the majority party in Lok Sabha.
questions.solution: The statement that the Prime Minister can be removed if a no-confidence motion is passed by both Houses with a 2/3rd majority is NOT correct. A no-confidence motion can only be introduced and passed in the Lok Sabha (Lower House) by a simple majority. If passed, the entire Council of Ministers, including the PM, must resign.

questions.question: Constitution Review Commission chaired by ______ recommended some initiatives to be taken by the government for successful implementation of Fundamental Duties.
questions.solution: The National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution (NCRWC), chaired by Justice M.N. Venkatachaliah (2000-2002), recommended several initiatives for the successful implementation of Fundamental Duties, such as incorporating them into school curriculums and sensitizing public servants.

questions.question: Who was the Prime Minister when Right to Property was scrapped as a Fundamental Right?
questions.solution: Morarji Desai was the Prime Minister (heading the Janata Party government) when the Right to Property was scrapped as a Fundamental Right by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978. It was subsequently shifted to Article 300A as a legal right.

questions.question: Fundamental Rights are protected and guaranteed by the ____ of the country.
questions.solution: Fundamental Rights are protected and guaranteed by the Constitution of the country. Unlike ordinary legal rights, which are protected by ordinary law, Fundamental Rights are the 'supreme law of the land' and cannot be taken away by the government except through a formal constitutional amendment.

questions.question: Article 76 of the Constitution of India deals with the office of the:
questions.solution: Article 76 provides for the office of the Attorney General of India. The Attorney General is the highest law officer in the country, appointed by the President. They have the right to speak in both Houses of Parliament but do not have the right to vote.

questions.question: In which town The Supreme Court was established for the First time under the Regulating Act of 1773?
questions.solution: The Supreme Court was established for the first time at Fort William, Calcutta, under the Regulating Act of 1773. It consisted of a Chief Justice (Sir Elijah Impey) and three other judges. This was the first major step toward a centralized judicial administration in British India.

questions.question: In the Indian political system, the real executive power is vested in:
questions.option_4: the Prime Minister and his Council of Ministers
questions.solution: In the Indian political system, while the President is the nominal executive, the real executive power is vested in the Prime Minister and his Council of Ministers. This is a core feature of the Parliamentary form of government, where the PM is the actual head of the government.

questions.question: The Indian judicial system is based on:
questions.solution: The Indian judicial system is a single integrated system. This means that unlike the US (where federal and state courts are separate), India has a hierarchy of courts with the Supreme Court at the top, followed by High Courts and Subordinate Courts, all enforcing both Central and State laws.

questions.question: From which country’s constitution has the Constitution of India borrowed the feature of Single Citizenship and Parliamentary system of Government?
questions.solution: The United Kingdom (UK) is the source for both Single Citizenship and the Parliamentary system of government. The Indian model is closely based on the British 'Westminster' system, characterized by the collective responsibility of the executive to the legislature.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution gives the right to a candidate, belonging to any caste, to apply for any of the public employment opportunities?
questions.solution: Article 16 (2) provides that no citizen shall, on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex, descent, place of birth, or residence, be ineligible for, or discriminated against in respect of, any employment or office under the State. It ensures equality of opportunity in public employment.

questions.question: When was National Emergency declared for the first time under Article 352?
questions.solution: The first National Emergency under Article 352 was declared in October 1962 due to Chinese aggression (Indo-China War) and lasted until January 1968. During this period, the security of India was declared to be threatened by external aggression.

questions.question: Which is NOT correct about the independence of the judiciary in our country?
questions.option_1: The legislature is not involved in the process of appointment of judges.
questions.option_2: The Constitution prescribes a very difficult procedure for removal of judges.
questions.option_3: The judges are financially dependent on both the executive and legislature for their salaries and allowances.
questions.option_4: The judiciary has the power to penalise those who are found guilty of contempt of court.
questions.solution: The statement that 'judges are financially dependent on the executive and legislature' is NOT correct. To ensure the independence of the judiciary, the salaries and allowances of judges are charged on the Consolidated Fund, meaning they are not subject to a vote in the legislature.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India deals with the appointment of ad-hoc judges?
questions.solution: Article 127 of the Constitution deals with the appointment of ad-hoc judges in the Supreme Court. If there is a lack of quorum of the permanent judges to hold or continue any session of the Court, the Chief Justice of India can appoint a High Court judge as an ad-hoc judge with the President's consent.

questions.question: By the 42nd Amendment in 1976, as introduced by the ______, the Chapter on the fundamental duties of citizens was incorporated into the Constitution.
questions.solution: The Swaran Singh Committee (1976) recommended the inclusion of Fundamental Duties. Based on these recommendations, the 42nd Amendment Act added a new Part IV-A and Article 51A to the Constitution. Note: The committee originally suggested eight duties, but ten were actually incorporated.

questions.question: The detention of a person cannot exceed ________ unless an advisory board consisting of judges of a High Court reports sufficient cause for extended detention.
questions.solution: Under Article 22, the detention of a person under a preventive detention law cannot exceed three months unless an Advisory Board (consisting of persons qualified to be High Court judges) finds sufficient cause for an extension. This serves as a vital check against arbitrary detention.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India deals with the Sessions of the Parliament?
questions.solution: Article 85 deals with the Sessions of Parliament, prorogation, and dissolution. It empowers the President to summon each House of Parliament to meet at such time and place as they think fit, provided that six months shall not intervene between two sessions.

questions.question: In which year was the Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Council abolished?
questions.solution: The Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Council was abolished in 2019 following the passage of the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019. This act reconstituted the state into two Union Territories (J&K and Ladakh) and transitioned J&K to a unicameral legislature.

questions.question: The principles of Liberty, Equality and Fraternity were adopted from the Constitution of:
questions.solution: The ideals of Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity in our Preamble were adopted from the French Constitution (specifically the French Revolution). These principles form the bedrock of social and political democracy in India.

questions.question: Which of the following was included by the Constitution (Eighty-sixth Amendment) Act, 2002?
questions.option_1: Readjustment of seats of the Lok Sabha
questions.option_4: Elementary education as a fundamental right
questions.solution: The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002 included Elementary education as a fundamental right by inserting Article 21A. It also made it a fundamental duty for parents (51A-k) and modified the Directive Principles (Art 45) regarding early childhood care.

questions.question: The idea of Rule of Law was adopted from the Constitution of which of the following countries?
questions.solution: The concept of the Rule of Law, which implies that no man is above the law and everyone is subject to the jurisdiction of ordinary courts, was adopted from the United Kingdom (specifically influenced by the writings of A.V. Dicey).

questions.question: The Sub-Section (C) in the list of Fundamental Duties requires an Indian citizen to uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and ______________ of India.
questions.solution: Article 51A (c) mandates every citizen to uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India. This duty emphasizes the importance of maintaining the territorial and social cohesion of the nation as a primary responsibility of its people.
